public_rationale: Testing completed on August 29, 2025, and published as a preprint on November 11 used blinded clinician ratings of responses to 158 prompts per product version, including GPT-5 Auto [e1]. GPT-5 Auto showed recurring inappropriate responses to psychotic content, supporting the prediction of material safety failures in an important application [e1]. OpenAI reported factuality gains in August 2025 and improved safety performance in October 2025, while acknowledging remaining failures [e2, e3]. Those improvements do not undo the failures documented in the August evaluation [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The decisive evidence is a preprint abstract, not a full reviewed study.
The evaluation concerns GPT-5 Auto and clinical appropriateness, not every GPT-5 configuration or every human value.
Results on selected psychotic prompts do not estimate failure rates in ordinary traffic.
The claim supplies no numerical reliability threshold.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, independently validated evaluations establish dependable compliance across ordinary and challenging uses, with only isolated, immaterial errors.

evidence.excerpt: No tested version of ChatGPT reliably generated appropriate responses to psychotic content.
evidence.locator: Abstract, Setting, Results, and Conclusions and relevance
evidence.explanation: Testing completed August 29 included GPT-5 Auto and used blinded clinician ratings of psychotic and control prompts. GPT-5 improved on the free product but still showed substantially elevated odds of inappropriate responses to psychotic prompts.
OpenAI reports substantial factuality gains on three benchmarks. This qualifies the extent of the problem but does not establish dependable compliance with the combined values claim.

evidence.excerpt: the model may not behave as intended
evidence.locator: What we found, Self harm and suicide
evidence.explanation: OpenAI reports improved performance after updating GPT-5, including 91% compliance on a challenging self-harm evaluation versus 77% previously. It also acknowledges remaining failures; these selected evaluations do not measure average user risk.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: Testing completed on this date systematically evaluated released GPT-5 Auto using blinded clinician ratings and found recurring material safety failures on psychotic content. The findings became public on November 11, 2025, satisfying the rule requiring a dated systematic evaluation rather than a single trivial mistake.
